case_title: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
facts_summary: The petitioner's minor daughter was kidnapped. Despite approaching the police authorities, an FIR was not registered for several days, citing informal preliminary inquiries.
legal_issues: Whether police officers have discretion to conduct a preliminary inquiry before registering an FIR under Section 154 CrPC when cognizable offence is disclosed?

ratio_decidendi: Registration of an FIR under Section 154 CrPC (Section 173 BNSS) is mandatory if the information discloses a cognizable offence. Preliminary inquiry is permissible only in exceptional cases (matrimonial, commercial fraud, medical negligence, corruption) within 7 days.

legal_issues: Whether an accused who was not arrested during investigation must inevitably be remanded to judicial custody upon filing of the chargesheet?

applicable_laws: Section 302 IPC (Section 103 BNS) & Section 3 Evidence Act
facts_summary: Death of a young bride by potassium cyanide poisoning within months of marriage. Case rested purely on circumstantial evidence without direct eyewitness testimony.
legal_issues: What is the standard of proof required to sustain a conviction for murder based solely on circumstantial evidence?
court_reasoning: A distance exists between 'may be true' and 'must be true'. The prosecution must travel all the way to prove guilt beyond all reasonable doubt.
ratio_decidendi: Established the 'Panchsheel' (Five Golden Principles) for circumstantial evidence: (1) Circumstances fully established, (2) Facts consistent only with hypothesis of guilt, (3) Conclusive nature, (4) Exclusion of every other hypothesis, (5) Chain of events complete with no gap.

applicable_laws: Section 67 NDPS Act & Section 25 Evidence Act (Section 23 BSA 2023)
facts_summary: Accused convicted of illicit trafficking of commercial quantity of ganja/charas primarily relying upon their confessional statements recorded by officers under Section 67 NDPS Act.

legal_issues: Whether conviction can be solely sustained on uncorroborated testimony of interested eyewitness?

facts_summary: Bail sought on grounds of parity as co-accused identically situated was granted bail by Coordinate Bench.
legal_issues: Whether gravity of offence alone is a sufficient ground to deny bail when trial will take substantial time?

case_title: State of Karnataka v. Santosh Shankar Jadhav
facts_summary: Banking loan availed with inflated collateral valuation certificates issued by panel surveyors.
legal_issues: Whether fraudulent intention existed at the inception of the transaction or arose subsequently?
court_reasoning: The original document was neither made nor signed by the applicant; mere possession without knowledge of forgery does not satisfy Section 471 IPC.
ratio_decidendi: A mere breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right from beginning.
